subject: AI & Agents
title: AlphaGo's Move 37
description: A quick, practical guide to AlphaGo's Move 37.

hook.text: Game 2, Move 37. The AI places a stone where no professional would. Commentators gasp. It's brilliant.

buildup.text: AlphaGo faced Lee Sedol, one of the greatest Go players in history, in a five-game match.

discovery.text: Move 37 was a shoulder hit on the fifth line — a move with a 1 in 10,000 probability by human standards.

twist.text: Fan Hui, the European champion, was commentating and said his hands were shaking watching it.

climax.text: The move turned the game. AlphaGo won the match 4-1 and changed how humans play Go forever.

punchline.text: One impossible move. A new chapter in human-machine history.

quiz.question: Why was AlphaGo's Move 37 so significant?
options: It was a move no human professional would play, yet it was brilliant
It was the fastest move in Go history
It was a copying of a famous historical game

details.summary: In 2016, AlphaGo shocked the world with Move 37 — a play no human expert would have considered. It defied centuries of Go strategy and won the game, proving AI can discover creative solutions beyond human intuition.
details.whyItMatters: Move 37 demonstrated that AI is not just fast — it can find strategies humans would never discover. It marked a turning point in AI creativity and strategic problem-solving.
takeaways: Move 37 was an unconventional play no expert predicted
AlphaGo discovered creative strategies beyond human Go knowledge
The moment proved AI can innovate, not just optimize

faq.question: Why was Move 37 so shocking to Go players?
faq.answer: Professional Go players considered it a mistake at first. The move violated centuries of established strategy. It turned out to be a brilliant play that secured AlphaGo's victory against world champion Lee Sedol.

faq.question: What made AlphaGo capable of discovering Move 37?
faq.answer: AlphaGo used a combination of deep neural networks and Monte Carlo tree search. By evaluating millions of positions, it found effective strategies that fell outside the patterns human players recognized.
